    86                  Proclamation 11061 of September 8, 2026
    87  
    88                  
    89  Excluding Certain Canadian Products From 
    90                  Importation Into the United States in Response to 
    91                  Continued Discrimination Against the Commerce of the 
    92                  United States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages
    93  
    94                  By the President of the United States of America
    95  
    96                  A Proclamation
    97  
    98                  1. In Proclamation 11046 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
    99                  Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination 
   100                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
   101                  to Alcoholic Beverages), I found as a fact that Canada 
   102                  is discriminating in fact against the commerce of the 
   103                  United States by banning the purchase, distribution, or 
   104                  retailing of U.S. alcoholic beverages while not banning 
   105                  or similarly restricting such products from other 
   106                  countries; that this discrimination places the commerce 
   107                  of the United States at a disadvantage compared to the 
   108                  commerce of other countries; and that Canada's 
   109                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
   110                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
   111                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States. 
   112                  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
   113                  from Canada's discrimination or unreasonable and 
   114                  unequal imposition on U.S. alcoholic beverages, I 
   115                  imposed under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 
   116                  U.S.C. 1338) (section 338) additional ad valorem 
   117                  duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain products 
   118                  of Canada.
   119  
   120                  2. In Proclamation 11056 of August 18, 2026 (Temporary 
   121                  Suspension of Additional Duties To Offset Canadian 
   122                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
   123                  States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, Dairy, and 
   124                  Motor Vehicles), I temporarily suspended for 3 days the 
   125                  effective date of the additional ad valorem duties 
   126                  imposed under Proclamation 11046 after Canada expressed 
   127                  a commitment to remove the discrimination or 
   128                  unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in 
   129                  Proclamation 11046.
   130  
   131                  3. On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its 
   132                  commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did 
   133                  not remove the discrimination or unreasonable and 
   134                  unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11046.
   135  
   136                  4. Accordingly, at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
   137                  22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 
   138                  11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties 
   139                  imposed under Proclamation 11046 became effective.
   140  
   141                  5. I have received certain information, opinions, and 
   142                  recommendations from senior executive branch officials 
   143                  on the status of the circumstances involved in 
   144                  Proclamation 11046 and of negotiations between the 
   145                  United States and Canada regarding the discrimination 
   146                  or imposition described in Proclamation 11046. 
   147                  According to senior executive branch officials, rather 
   148                  than remove Canada's discriminatory treatment of or 
   149                  unreasonable and unequal imposition on U.S. alcoholic 
   150                  beverages, Canadian authorities maintained the 
   151                  discrimination and announced additional retaliation 
   152                  against the United States related to U.S. alcoholic 
   153                  beverages. For example, on August 27, 2026, the 
   154                  Government of Saskatchewan--which is one of two 
   155                  provinces that at the time of the signing of 
   156                  Proclamation 11046 and the effective date of the 
   157                  additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 
   158                  11046 did not outright ban U.S. alcoholic beverages--
   159                  announced that it would impose an additional 50 percent 
   160                  levy on U.S. alcoholic beverages, effective September 
   161                  8, 2026, expressly
   162  
   163  [[Page 58312]]
   164  
   165                  in response to the additional ad valorem duties imposed 
   166                  in Proclamation 11046. In my senior executive branch 
   167                  officials' opinion, an import ban on certain Canadian 
   168                  alcoholic beverages currently subject to the additional 
   169                  ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046 is 
   170                  consistent with the interests of the United States and 
   171                  the public interests.
   172  
   173                  6. After considering the information, opinions, and 
   174                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
   175                  executive branch officials, among other relevant 
   176                  information and considerations, I find it to be a fact 
   177                  that Canada has, after the issuance of Proclamation 
   178                  11046 and after the additional ad valorem duties 
   179                  imposed in Proclamation 11046 became effective, 
   180                  maintained or increased the discriminations against the 
   181                  commerce of the United States described in Proclamation 
   182                  11046.
   183  
   184                  7. I determine that it is consistent with the interests 
   185                  of the United States to issue this further proclamation 
   186                  directing that certain products of Canada that are 
   187                  currently subject to the additional ad valorem duties 
   188                  imposed in Proclamation 11046 be excluded from 
   189                  importation into the United States. I determine that it 
   190                  is consistent with the public interests to exclude from 
   191                  importation into the United States certain alcoholic 
   192                  beverages of Canada that are currently subject to the 
   193                  additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 
   194                  11046, as further detailed in the Annex to this 
   195                  proclamation.
   196  
   197                  8. In my judgment, the action in this proclamation is 
   198                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   199                  of the United States, is required by the public 
   200                  interests, and will serve the public interest.
   201  
   202                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   203                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   204                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   205                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   206                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   207                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   208                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   209                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   210                  finding that a foreign country is imposing an 
   211                  unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or 
   212                  limitation that is not equally enforced on the like 
   213                  articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in 
   214                  fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the 
   215                  commerce of the United States at a disadvantage 
   216                  compared to the commerce of any foreign country. 
   217                  Section 338 also authorizes the President to suspend, 
   218                  revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under 
   219                  section 338 whenever the President deems that the 
   220                  public interests require such action. Further, section 
   221                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   222                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   223                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   224                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   225                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   226                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   227                  of the United States.
   228  
   229                  10. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
   230                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   231                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule 
   232                  of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes 
   233                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   234                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   235                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   236                  restriction.
   237  
   238                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   239                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   240                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   241                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   242                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   243                  follows:
   244  
   245  (1) Except as otherwise provided in this proclamation, certain alcoholic 
   246  beverages that are products of Canada, as set forth in the Annex to this 
   247  proclamation, are excluded from importation into the United States, 
   248  effective with respect to goods imported on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern 
   249  time on September 29, 2026.
   250  
   251  (2) Products that will be subject to the import ban in this proclamation 
   252  that were imported, but not yet entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   253  warehouse for consumption, prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject 
   254  to the 50 percent duty rate established by Proclamation 11046.
   255  
   256  [[Page 58313]]
   257  
   258  (3) Besides changing certain products from being subject to the additional 
   259  ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11046 to being subject to the 
   260  import ban set forth in this proclamation, this proclamation does not 
   261  otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation 
   262  of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to 
   263  the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the 
   264  Commerce of the United States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages), that 
   265  are subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 
   266  11046.
   267  
   268  (4) The head of each executive department and agency (agency) is authorized 
   269  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   270  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   271  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   272  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   273  agency.
   274  
   275  (5) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in 
   276  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, 
   277  and the United States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue such 
   278  rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or determinations as may be 
   279  necessary to implement this proclamation and is authorized to take any 
   280  necessary measures to administer the import ban imposed in this 
   281  proclamation.
   282  
   283  (6) The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with the Secretary of the 
   284  Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the United States Trade 
   285  Representative, the Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   286  Commission, and any other senior executive branch official he deems 
   287  appropriate, shall determine whether any additional modifications to the 
   288  HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation and shall make such 
   289  modifications to the HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register, 
   290  including any technical or ministerial correction to the Annex to this 
   291  proclamation.
   292  
   293  (7) For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of CBP makes to implement 
   294  this proclamation, the Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by 
   295  law, obtain the approval of the President or the United States Trade 
   296  Representative. The United States Trade Representative is delegated the 
   297  President's approval authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).
   298  
   299  (8) Any provision of previous proclamations and Executive Orders that is 
   300  inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   301  inconsistency.
   302  
   303  (9)(a) If any provision of this proclamation or the application of any 
   304  provision to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the 
   305  remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any 
   306  other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.
   307  
   308    (b) If the import ban imposed in this proclamation is invalidated in 
   309  whole or in part as to any import, then the 50 percent ad valorem duty 
   310  imposed in Proclamation 11046 shall apply to the import to which the 
   311  invalidated import ban or the invalidated part of the import ban had 
   312  applied before its invalidation. No other import ban imposed in this 
   313  proclamation shall be affected, and no additional ad valorem duty imposed 
   314  in Proclamation 11046 or a proclamation issued subsequent to Proclamation 
   315  11046 shall be affected. This severability provision, including its 
   316  operative effect if triggered, is consistent with the public interests and 
   317  the interests of the United States, is required by the public interests, 
   318  and will serve the public interest.
   319  
   320  [[Page 58314]]
   321  
   322                  IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this 
   323                  eighth day of September, in the year of our Lord two 
   324                  thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the 
   325                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-
   326                  first.

    29                  United States With Respect to Dairy
    30  
    31                  By the President of the United States of America
    32  
    33                  A Proclamation
    34  
    35                  1. In Proclamation 11047 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing 
    36                  Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination 
    37                  Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect 
    38                  to Dairy), I found as a fact that Canada is 
    39                  discriminating in fact against the commerce of the 
    40                  United States through Canada's tariff-rate quota 
    41                  allocation measures imposed on U.S. cheeses of all 
    42                  types; that this discrimination places the commerce of 
    43                  the United States at a disadvantage compared to the 
    44                  commerce of other countries; and that Canada's 
    45                  imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced 
    46                  upon the like articles of every foreign country, and 
    47                  places a burden on the commerce of the United States. 
    48                  To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce 
    49                  from Canada's discrimination or unreasonable and 
    50                  unequal imposition on U.S. dairy, I imposed under 
    51                  section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1338) 
    52                  (section 338) additional ad valorem duties, effective 
    53                  August 19, 2026, on certain products of Canada.
    54  
    55                  2. In Proclamation 11056 of August 18, 2026 (Temporary 
    56                  Suspension of Additional Duties To Offset Canadian 
    57                  Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United 
    58                  States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, Dairy, and 
    59                  Motor Vehicles), I temporarily suspended for 3 days the 
    60                  effective date of the additional ad valorem duties 
    61                  imposed under Proclamation 11047 after Canada expressed 
    62                  a commitment to remove the discrimination or 
    63                  unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in 
    64                  Proclamation 11047.
    65  
    66                  3. On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its 
    67                  commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did 
    68                  not remove the discrimination or unreasonable and 
    69                  unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11047.

    71                  4. Accordingly, at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 
    72                  22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 
    73                  11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties 
    74                  imposed under Proclamation 11047 became effective.
    75  
    76                  5. I have received certain information, opinions, and 
    77                  recommendations from senior executive branch officials 
    78                  on the status of the circumstances involved in 
    79                  Proclamation 11047 and of negotiations between the 
    80                  United States and Canada regarding the discrimination 
    81                  or imposition described in Proclamation 11047. 
    82                  According to senior executive branch officials, after 
    83                  the issuance of Proclamation 11047 and after the 
    84                  additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 
    85                  11047 became effective, Canada did not revoke its 
    86                  tariff-rate quota allocation measures involving dairy 
    87                  but has maintained the discrimination or unreasonable 
    88                  and unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11047. 
    89                  In my senior executive branch officials' opinion, an 
    90                  import ban on certain Canadian products currently 
    91                  subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in 
    92                  Proclamation 11047 is consistent with the interests of 
    93                  the United States and the public interests.

    95                  6. After considering the information, opinions, and 
    96                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
    97                  executive branch officials, among other
    98  
    99  [[Page 58320]]
   100  
   101                  relevant information and considerations, I find it to 
   102                  be a fact that Canada has, after the issuance of 
   103                  Proclamation 11047 and after the additional ad valorem 
   104                  duties imposed in Proclamation 11047 became effective, 
   105                  maintained the discriminations against the commerce of 
   106                  the United States described in Proclamation 11047.
   107  
   108                  7. I determine that it is consistent with the interests 
   109                  of the United States to issue this further proclamation 
   110                  directing that certain products of Canada shall be 
   111                  excluded from importation into the United States. I 
   112                  determine that it is consistent with the public 
   113                  interests to exclude from importation into the United 
   114                  States certain products of Canada that are currently 
   115                  subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in 
   116                  Proclamation 11047, as further detailed in the Annex to 
   117                  this proclamation.

   119                  8. In my judgment, the action in this proclamation is 
   120                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   121                  of the United States, is required by the public 
   122                  interests, and will serve the public interest.

   124                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   125                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   126                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   127                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   128                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   129                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   130                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   131                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   132                  finding that a foreign country is imposing an 
   133                  unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or 
   134                  limitation that is not equally enforced on the like 
   135                  articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in 
   136                  fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the 
   137                  commerce of the United States at a disadvantage 
   138                  compared to the commerce of any foreign country. 
   139                  Section 338 also authorizes the President to suspend, 
   140                  revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under 
   141                  section 338 whenever the President deems that the 
   142                  public interests require such action. Further, section 
   143                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   144                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   145                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   146                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   147                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   148                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   149                  of the United States.

   152                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   153                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule

   155                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   156                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   157                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   158                  restriction.

   160                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   161                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   162                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   163                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   164                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   165                  follows:

   168  Canada, as set forth in the Annex to this proclamation, are excluded from 
   169  importation into the United States, effective with respect to goods 
   170  imported on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on September 29, 2026.

   173  that were imported, but not yet entered for consumption, or withdrawn from 
   174  warehouse for consumption, prior to September 29, 2026, will remain subject

   178  ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11047 to being subject to the

   189  to and shall take all appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   190  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency may, consistent with 
   191  applicable law, including section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
   192  redelegate the authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   193  agency.
   194  
   195  (5) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), in 
   196  consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, 
   197  and the United States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue such 
   198  rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or determinations as may be 
   199  necessary to implement this proclamation and is authorized to take any 
   200  necessary measures to administer the import ban imposed in this 
   201  proclamation.
   202

   204  Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, the United States Trade 
   205  Representative, the Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   206  Commission, and any other senior executive branch official he deems

   208  HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation and shall make such 
   209  modifications to the HTSUS through notice in the Federal Register, 
   210  including any technical or ministerial correction to the Annex to this 
   211  proclamation.

   214  this proclamation, the Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by 
   215  law, obtain the approval of the President or the United States Trade 
   216  Representative. The United States Trade Representative is delegated the 
   217  President's approval authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).

   220  inconsistent with this proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   221  inconsistency.

   224  provision to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the 
   225  remainder of this proclamation and the application of its provisions to any 
   226  other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.

   229  whole or in part as to any import, then the 50 percent ad valorem duty 
   230  imposed in Proclamation 11047 shall apply to the import to which the

   234  in Proclamation 11047 or a proclamation issued subsequent to Proclamation 
   235  11047 shall be affected. This severability provision, including its 
   236  operative effect if triggered, is consistent with the public interests and

   238  and will serve the public interest.
   239

   241  
   242                  IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this 
   243                  eighth day of September, in the year of our Lord two 
   244                  thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the 
   245                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

   127                  11048, as amended, including how effectively those 
   128                  duties are offsetting the burden or disadvantage on 
   129                  U.S. commerce. According to senior executive branch 
   130                  officials, although the additional ad valorem duties 
   131                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, offset the 
   132                  burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce, modifying the 
   133                  scope of products
   134  
   135  [[Page 68862]]
   136  
   137                  subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in 
   138                  Proclamation 11048, as amended, would still offset the 
   139                  burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better 
   140                  serve the public interest. In my senior executive 
   141                  branch officials' opinion, modifying the scope of 
   142                  products subject to the additional ad valorem duties 
   143                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, is required 
   144                  by the public interests and is consistent with the 
   145                  interests of the United States.
   146  
   147                  7. After considering the information, opinions, and 
   148                  recommendations that have been provided to me by senior 
   149                  executive branch officials, among other relevant 
   150                  information and considerations, I determine that the 
   151                  public interests require modifying the scope of 
   152                  products subject to the additional ad valorem duties 
   153                  imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended.
   154  
   155                  8. In my judgment, the modification in this 
   156                  proclamation will offset the burden or disadvantage on 
   157                  U.S. commerce, is consistent with the public interests 
   158                  and the interests of the United States, is required by 
   159                  the public interests, and will better serve the public 
   160                  interest.
   161  
   162                  9. Section 338 authorizes the President, if he 
   163                  determines it will serve the public interest, to offset 
   164                  any burden or disadvantage placed on the commerce of 
   165                  the United States by an unequal imposition or 
   166                  discrimination by a foreign country by specifying and 
   167                  declaring additional duties not to exceed 50 percent ad 
   168                  valorem (or its equivalent) and not to take effect 
   169                  earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation 
   170                  finding that a foreign country is imposing an 
   171                  unreasonable charge, exaction, regulation, or 
   172                  limitation that is not equally enforced on the like 
   173                  articles of every foreign country, or discriminates in 
   174                  fact against U.S. commerce in a way that places the 
   175                  commerce of the United States at a disadvantage 
   176                  compared to the commerce of any foreign country. 
   177                  Section 338 also authorizes the President to suspend, 
   178                  revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under 
   179                  section 338 whenever the President deems that the 
   180                  public interests require such action. Further, section 
   181                  338 authorizes the President to exclude from 
   182                  importation articles of the foreign country if the 
   183                  foreign country maintains or increases the 
   184                  discrimination against the commerce of the United 
   185                  States and the President deems the exclusion to be 
   186                  consistent with the public interests and the interests 
   187                  of the United States.
   188  
   189                  10. Section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended 
   190                  (19 U.S.C. 2483) (section 604), authorizes the 
   191                  President to embody in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule 
   192                  of the United States (HTSUS) the substance of statutes 
   193                  affecting import treatment, and actions thereunder, 
   194                  including the removal, modification, continuance, or 
   195                  imposition of any rate of duty or other import 
   196                  restriction.
   197  
   198                  NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the 
   199                  United States of America, by the authority vested in me 
   200                  by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, 
   201                  including section 338; section 301 of title 3, United 
   202                  States Code; and section 604, do hereby proclaim as 
   203                  follows:
   204  
   205                      (1) Except as otherwise provided in this 
   206                  proclamation, certain products of Canada, as set forth 
   207                  in Annex I, Part A to this proclamation, imported into 
   208                  the United States shall no longer be subject to the 
   209                  additional ad valorem duty of 50 percent imposed 
   210                  pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended. In 
   211                  addition, certain products of Canada, as set forth in 
   212                  Annex I, Part B to this proclamation, imported into the 
   213                  United States shall be subject to the additional ad 
   214                  valorem duty of 50 percent imposed pursuant to 
   215                  Proclamation 11048, as amended. The duties imposed 
   216                  pursuant to Proclamation 11048, as amended, and as 
   217                  modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition 
   218                  to duties imposed pursuant to section 232 of the Trade 
   219                  Expansion Act of 1962, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1862). 
   220                  These changes shall be effective with respect to goods 
   221                  entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   222                  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   223                  October 30, 2026.
   224                      (2) The HTSUS is modified as provided in Annex II 
   225                  to this proclamation, effective with respect to goods 
   226                  entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   227                  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   228                  October 30, 2026, and the modifications shall continue 
   229                  in effect unless this action is expressly suspended, 
   230                  revoked, supplemented, amended, or terminated.
   231  
   232  [[Page 68863]]
   233  
   234                      (3) The head of each executive department and 
   235                  agency (agency) is authorized to and shall take all 
   236                  appropriate measures within the agency's authority to 
   237                  implement this proclamation. The head of each agency 
   238                  may, consistent with applicable law, including section 
   239                  301 of title 3, United States Code, redelegate the 
   240                  authority to take such appropriate measures within the 
   241                  agency.
   242                      (4) The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border 
   243                  Protection (CBP), in consultation with the Secretary of 
   244                  the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the United 
   245                  States Trade Representative, is authorized to issue 
   246                  such rules, regulations, guidance, instructions, or 
   247                  determinations as may be necessary to implement this 
   248                  proclamation and is authorized to take any necessary 
   249                  measures to administer this proclamation.
   250                      (5) The Commissioner of CBP, in consultation with 
   251                  the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of 
   252                  Commerce, the United States Trade Representative, the 
   253                  Chairman of the United States International Trade 
   254                  Commission, and any other senior executive branch 
   255                  official the Commissioner of CBP deems appropriate, 
   256                  shall determine whether any additional modifications to 
   257                  the HTSUS are necessary to effectuate this proclamation 
   258                  and shall make such modifications to the HTSUS through 
   259                  notice in the Federal Register, including any technical 
   260                  or ministerial correction to the annexes to this 
   261                  proclamation.
   262                      (6) For any rule or regulation the Commissioner of 
   263                  CBP makes to implement this proclamation, the 
   264                  Commissioner of CBP shall, to the extent required by 
   265                  law, obtain the approval of the President or the United 
   266                  States Trade Representative. The United States Trade 
   267                  Representative is delegated the President's approval 
   268                  authority in 19 U.S.C. 1338(h).
   269                      (7) Any provision of previous proclamations and 
   270                  Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this 
   271                  proclamation is superseded to the extent of such 
   272                  inconsistency.
   273                      (8) If any provision of this proclamation or the 
   274                  application of any provision to any individual or 
   275                  circumstance is held to be invalid, the remainder of 
   276                  this proclamation and the application of its provisions 
   277                  to any other individuals or circumstances shall not be 
   278                  affected.
   279  
   280                  IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this 
   281                  twenty-third day of October, in the year of our Lord 
   282                  two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the 
   283                  United States of America the two hundred and fifty-
   284                  first.

    23                  Memorandum of July 23, 2026
    24  
    25                  
    26  Actions by the United States in the 
    27                  Investigations Under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 
    28                  1974 of the Acts, Policies, and Practices of 60 
    29                  Economies Related to the Failure of Each Economy To 
    30                  Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the 
    31                  Importation of Goods Produced With Forced Labor
    32  
    33                  Memorandum for the United States Trade Representative
    34  
    35                  On March 12, 2026, the United States Trade 
    36                  Representative (Trade Representative) initiated 
    37                  investigations under section 301 of the Trade Act of 
    38                  1974, as amended (19 U.S.C. 2411) (section 301), into 
    39                  the acts, policies, and practices of 60 economies to 
    40                  examine whether any of the economies subject to these 
    41                  investigations fail to prohibit or to effectively 
    42                  enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods 
    43                  produced wholly or in part with forced labor and 
    44                  whether the failure is unreasonable or discriminatory 
    45                  and burdens or restricts U.S. commerce. 91 Fed. Reg. 
    46                  12884 (Initiation of Section 301 Investigations). The 
    47                  economies subject to these investigations are:
    48  
    49                      1. Algeria
    50                      2. Angola
    51                      3. Argentina
    52                      4. Australia
    53                      5. The Bahamas
    54                      6. Bahrain
    55                      7. Bangladesh
    56                      8. Brazil
    57                      9. Cambodia
    58                      10. Canada
    59                      11. Chile
    60                      12. China, People's Republic of
    61                      13. Colombia
    62                      14. Costa Rica
    63                      15. Dominican Republic
    64                      16. Ecuador
    65                      17. Egypt
    66                      18. El Salvador
    67                      19. European Union
    68                      20. Guatemala
    69                      21. Guyana
    70                      22. Honduras
    71                      23. Hong Kong, China
    72                      24. India
    73  
    74  [[Page 47718]]
    75  
    76                      25. Indonesia
    77                      26. Iraq
    78                      27. Israel
    79                      28. Japan
    80                      29. Jordan
    81                      30. Kazakhstan
    82                      31. Kuwait
    83                      32. Libya
    84                      33. Malaysia
    85                      34. Mexico
    86                      35. Morocco
    87                      36. New Zealand
    88                      37. Nicaragua
    89                      38. Nigeria
    90                      39. Norway
    91                      40. Oman
    92                      41. Pakistan
    93                      42. Peru
    94                      43. Philippines
    95                      44. Qatar
    96                      45. Russia
    97                      46. Saudi Arabia
    98                      47. Singapore
    99                      48. South Africa
   100                      49. South Korea
   101                      50. Sri Lanka
   102                      51. Switzerland
   103                      52. Taiwan
   104                      53. Thailand
   105                      54. Trinidad and Tobago
   106                      55. T[uuml]rkiye
   107                      56. United Arab Emirates
   108                      57. United Kingdom
   109                      58. Uruguay
   110                      59. Venezuela
   111                      60. Vietnam
   112  
   113                  On June 2, 2026, the Trade Representative determined 
   114                  that the acts, policies, and practices of each of these 
   115                  economies are unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. 
   116                  commerce and thus are actionable under section 
   117                  301(b)(1) (19 U.S.C. 2411(b)(1)) (Notice of 
   118                  Determinations: 2026-11296; 91 Fed. Reg. 34272) (Notice 
   119                  of Determinations).
   120  
   121                  As a result of these determinations, the Trade 
   122                  Representative proposed to determine in each 
   123                  investigation that action is appropriate under section 
   124                  301 to obtain the elimination of the actionable acts, 
   125                  policies, and practices, including imposing ad valorem 
   126                  tariffs on all goods of each investigated economy, with 
   127                  exemptions for certain goods. To obtain the elimination
   128  
   129  [[Page 47719]]
   130  
   131                  of the actionable acts, policies, and practices in each 
   132                  investigation, the Trade Representative proposed 
   133                  section 301 tariffs. The Trade Representative proposed 
   134                  tariffs of 10 percent ad valorem on goods of economies 
   135                  that: impose a forced labor import prohibition but do 
   136                  not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, the 
   137                  European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and Pakistan); have 
   138                  undertaken commitments in their respective Agreements 
   139                  on Reciprocal Trade regarding forced labor import 
   140                  prohibitions (Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, 
   141                  El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, and 
   142                  Taiwan); or have imposed a partial regime with the 
   143                  effect of preventing the importation of certain forced 
   144                  labor goods (the United Kingdom). For all other 
   145                  economies whose failure to impose forced labor import 
   146                  prohibitions the Trade Representative has found 
   147                  actionable under section 301, the Trade Representative 
   148                  proposed section 301 tariffs of 12.5 percent ad 
   149                  valorem. In addition, the Trade Representative proposed 
   150                  to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a 
   151                  certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter 
   152                  the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate.
   153  
   154                  The Office of the United States Trade Representative 
   155                  (USTR) invited comments by interested persons on these 
   156                  proposed actions and convened public hearings on July 
   157                  7, 8, and 9, 2026. USTR received over 1,600 written 
   158                  comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses at the 
   159                  hearings.
   160  
   161                  The Trade Representative has informed me of the 
   162                  substance of significant comments on the proposed 
   163                  actions in each investigation and provided me his 
   164                  advice on appropriate actions, including tariffs of 
   165                  various rates, exemptions for certain products, and 
   166                  tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) for specific types of 
   167                  products for certain economies. For example, the Trade 
   168                  Representative advised me that after considering the 
   169                  comments and testimony received, certain products 
   170                  warrant exemption from tariffs imposed in connection 
   171                  with an investigation, including because of the needs 
   172                  of the U.S. economy or based on the extent to which 
   173                  imposing tariffs on the products will contribute to the 
   174                  elimination of the acts, policies, and practices of the 
   175                  economies found to be actionable in the investigations 
   176                  described above. These exemptions encompass (a) raw 
   177                  materials that if subject to the proposed additional 
   178                  tariffs could lead to the unavailability of domestic 
   179                  supply; (b) products that could cause economy-wide 
   180                  disruptions if subject to the proposed additional 
   181                  tariffs; (c) products that cannot be grown or produced 
   182                  in sufficient quantities or at reasonable prices in the 
   183                  United States or obtained from other sources; (d) 
   184                  products that if exempted from these tariffs would 
   185                  encourage economies that have made commitments to the 
   186                  United States regarding forced labor import 
   187                  prohibitions to implement those commitments or to enact 
   188                  and effectively enforce a forced labor import 
   189                  prohibition; or (e) articles for which these tariffs 
   190                  may not contribute substantially to the elimination of 
   191                  the acts, policies, and practices of the economies 
   192                  found to be actionable in the investigations described 
   193                  above.
   194  
   195                  The Trade Representative has also advised me that for 
   196                  goods of the European Union, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, 
   197                  or Taiwan, section 301 tariffs that are the net of 
   198                  Most-Favored Nation (MFN) tariffs would be consistent 
   199                  with their respective Agreements on Reciprocal Trade or 
   200                  similar arrangements and would be appropriate to 
   201                  encourage these economies to fulfill commitments 
   202                  regarding forced labor import prohibitions or to enact 
   203                  or effectively enforce such a prohibition.
   204  
   205                  Further, the Trade Representative has advised me that, 
   206                  based on the comments and testimony received, the 
   207                  establishment of TRQs on certain textile and apparel 
   208                  goods is appropriate as a means to encourage the 
   209                  importation by trading partners of U.S. cotton and 
   210                  textile goods, in order to reduce the reliance of such 
   211                  partners on inputs from other sources that are more 
   212                  likely to contain forced labor inputs. Such TRQs, in 
   213                  combination with other tariffs on other products of 
   214                  those trading partners, are appropriate to obtain the 
   215                  elimination of the acts, policies, or practices found 
   216                  actionable under section 301 for those trading 
   217                  partners. The Trade Representative has also
   218  
   219  [[Page 47720]]
   220  
   221                  informed me that establishing these TRQs is not 
   222                  feasible at this time, but that establishing these TRQs 
   223                  will be feasible by September 1, 2026.
   224  
   225                  Finally, the Trade Representative has informed me that 
   226                  following consultation with certain economies in these 
   227                  investigations and publication of the Notice of 
   228                  Determinations, additional economies have imposed 
   229                  forced labor import prohibitions (Cambodia, Guatemala, 
   230                  Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, and Trinidad and Tobago) or 
   231                  undertaken commitments regarding forced labor import 
   232                  prohibitions in an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade 
   233                  (Jordan). As a result of these actions, the Trade 
   234                  Representative has advised me that the goods of these 
   235                  economies should be tariffed at the 10 percent rate to 
   236                  further encourage these economies to effectively 
   237                  enforce such prohibitions, and, in the case of Jordan, 
   238                  to enact and effectively enforce its commitments 
   239                  regarding forced labor import prohibitions.
   240  
   241                  After considering the relevant issues and factors and 
   242                  weighing the relevant considerations, including this 
   243                  information and advice from the Trade Representative; 
   244                  the information, findings, and determinations in USTR's 
   245                  Notice of Determinations; and the need to obtain the 
   246                  elimination of the acts, policies, and practices of the 
   247                  investigated economies found to be actionable under 
   248                  section 301, it is hereby directed as follows:
   249  
   250                  Section 1. Tariffs and Exemptions. (a) Except as 
   251                  otherwise provided in this memorandum, the Trade 
   252                  Representative shall impose the following tariff rates 
   253                  on all goods of the economy for which an act, policy, 
   254                  or practice was found actionable under section 301:
   255  
   256  (i) 10 percent tariff rate: The Trade Representative shall impose a tariff 
   257  of 10 percent on goods of Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Canada, Ecuador, 
   258  El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, 
   259  Mexico, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the United Kingdom, and Trinidad and Tobago.
   260  
   261  (ii) Tariff rate of 10 percent or 12.5 percent, net of MFN rate: For a 
   262  product of the European Union or Taiwan, where such product's MFN tariff is 
   263  less than 10 percent, the Trade Representative shall impose a section 301 
   264  tariff pursuant to these investigations so that the sum of the MFN tariff 
   265  and the section 301 tariff shall be 10 percent, and where such product's 
   266  MFN tariff is greater than or equal to 10 percent, the Trade Representative 
   267  shall impose a section 301 tariff of zero. For a product of Japan, Korea, 
   268  or Switzerland, where such product's MFN tariff is less than 12.5 percent, 
   269  the Trade Representative shall impose a section 301 tariff pursuant to 
   270  these investigations so that the sum of the MFN tariff and the tariff 
   271  imposed pursuant to these investigations shall be 12.5 percent, and where 
   272  such product's MFN tariff is greater than or equal to 12.5 percent, the 
   273  Trade Representative shall impose a section 301 tariff of zero. Capping 
   274  total duties in this manner is feasible, consistent with the terms of the 
   275  Agreements on Reciprocal Trade or similar arrangements, and appropriate to 
   276  encourage these economies to fulfill commitments regarding forced labor 
   277  import prohibitions or to enact and effectively enforce such a prohibition.
   278  
   279  (iii) 12.5 percent tariff rate: For goods of all other investigated 
   280  economies, the Trade Representative shall impose a tariff rate of 12.5 
   281  percent.
   282  
   283                      (b) The Trade Representative shall exempt from the 
   284                  tariffs imposed as directed in subsection (a) of this 
   285                  section the products identified in the Annex to this 
   286                  memorandum for each economy for which an act, policy, 
   287                  or practice was found actionable under section 301, as 
   288                  the products identified constitute:
   289  
   290  (i) raw materials that if subject to these tariffs could lead to the 
   291  unavailability of domestic supply;
   292  
   293  (ii) products that could cause economy-wide disruptions if subject to these 
   294  tariffs;
   295  
   296  (iii) products that cannot be grown or produced in sufficient quantities in 
   297  the United States or obtained from other sources;
   298  
   299  [[Page 47721]]
   300  
   301  (iv) products for which these tariffs may not be effective in obtaining the 
   302  elimination of the acts, policies, and practices of economies found to be 
   303  actionable in the investigations; or
   304  
   305  (v) certain products of Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El 
   306  Salvador, the European Union, Guatemala, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, 
   307  Switzerland, Taiwan, or the United Kingdom that would encourage these 
   308  economies to fulfill commitments regarding forced labor import prohibitions 
   309  or to encourage these economies to enact and effectively enforce a forced 
   310  labor import prohibition.
   311  
   312                      (c) After considering the relevant issues and 
   313                  factors and weighing the relevant considerations, 
   314                  including potential economic harm and efficacy of 
   315                  tariffs, I determine that the products identified in 
   316                  the Annex to this memorandum shall be exempted from the 
   317                  tariffs directed in subsection (a) of this section, and 
   318                  the Trade Representative shall direct that the 
   319                  Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) 
   320                  be modified as provided in the Annex to this 
   321                  memorandum. In my judgment, the tariffs directed in 
   322                  subsection (a) of this section with the exemptions 
   323                  described in subsection (b) of this section are 
   324                  appropriate and feasible to obtain the elimination of 
   325                  the acts, policies, or practices of the economies found 
   326                  to be actionable under section 301.
   327  
   328                  Sec. 2. Tariff-Rate Quotas. (a) As soon as the Trade 
   329                  Representative determines that it is feasible, the 
   330                  Trade Representative shall:
   331  
   332  (i) establish TRQs for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, with 
   333  an initial duration of 3 years, to encourage the importation by each of 
   334  these economies of U.S. textile goods, in order to reduce reliance on 
   335  inputs from other sources that are more likely to contain forced labor 
   336  inputs; and
   337  
   338  (ii) structure the TRQs for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia 
   339  to allow for a certain volume of specific textiles and apparel, based on 
   340  that economy's importation of U.S. inputs, to enter the United States free 
   341  of the section 301 tariffs provided for in section 1(a) of this memorandum.
   342  
   343                      (b) As soon as the Trade Representative determines 
   344                  that it is feasible, the Trade Representative shall:
   345  
   346  (i) establish TRQs for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, with

    64  Notice of Actions in Section 301 Investigations of Acts, 
    65  Policies, and Practices of Various Economies Related to the Failure of 
    66  Each Economy To Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the 
    67  Importation of Goods Produced With Forced Labor
    68  
    69  AGENCY: Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR).
    70  
    71  ACTION: Notice of action.
    72  
    73  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    74  
    75  SUMMARY: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) 
    76  has determined under Section 301(b) and Section 304(a) of the Trade Act 
    77  of 1974, as amended (Trade Act), that in each of 60 investigations, 
    78  certain of the acts, policies, and practices of the economy at issue 
    79  are actionable and that action by the United States is appropriate. In 
    80  accordance with the specific direction of the President, the Trade 
    81  Representative is taking actions in each of these investigations by 
    82  imposing tariffs on all products of the investigated economy, with 
    83  certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II to this notice 
    84  (Notice). Consistent with the specific direction of the President, for 
    85  an economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition, has 
    86  committed to impose and enforce such a prohibition through an Agreement 
    87  on Reciprocal Trade (ART), or has imposed a partial regime with the 
    88  effect of preventing the importation of certain forced labor goods, the 
    89  Trade Representative has determined 10 percent is the appropriate rate 
    90  of Section 301 duties, with specific economies subject to a 10 percent 
    91  rate net of a product's most-favored-nation (MFN) duty. For every other 
    92  economy, and in accordance with the specific direction of the 
    93  President, the Trade Representative has determined 12.5 percent is the 
    94  appropriate rate of Section 301 duty, with specific economies subject 
    95  to a 12.5 percent rate net of a product's MFN duty. The Trade 
    96  Representative has also determined, consistent with the specific 
    97  direction of the President, to establish, when feasible, tariff-rate 
    98  quotas (TRQs) for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, based 
    99  on each economy's importation of U.S. inputs, to encourage the 
   100  importation by each of these economies of U.S. cotton and textile 
   101  goods, in order to reduce reliance on inputs from other sources that 
   102  are more likely to contain forced labor inputs.
   103  
   104  DATES: The additional rates of duty are applicable with respect to 
   105  products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse 
   106  for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, 
   107  except that goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in 
   108  transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on 
   109  July 24, 2026, and entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse 
   110  for consumption before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall 
   111  not be subject to such additional duty.
   112  
   113  FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: For general questions about this 
   114  Notice, contact Megan Grimball and Philip Butler, Chairs of the Section 
   115  301 Committee, at (202) 395-5725.
   116  
   117  SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
   118  
   119  I. Proceedings in the Investigations
   120  
   121      On March 12, 2026, the Trade Representative initiated 60 
   122  investigations related to the failure of various economies to each 
   123  impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of 
   124  goods produced wholly or in part with forced labor (forced labor import 
   125  prohibition), pursuant to 302(b)(1) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 
   126  2412(b)(1)). See 91 FR 12884 (published March 17, 2026).
   127      On June 2, 2026, the Trade Representative determined that, in each 
   128  of the 60 investigations, certain of the acts, polices, and practices 
   129  of the economy at issue are actionable under sections 301(b) and 304(a) 
   130  of the Trade Act. The Trade Representative also issued a comprehensive 
   131  report, Acts, Policies, and Practices of Various Economies Related to 
   132  the Failure to Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the 
   133  Importation of Goods Produced with Forced Labor (Report). Specifically, 
   134  the Trade Representative determined that:
   135       The following 54 economies have failed to impose and 
   136  effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced 
   137  with forced labor: Algeria; Angola; Argentina; Australia; the Bahamas; 
   138  Bahrain; Bangladesh; Brazil; Cambodia; Chile; China, People's Republic 
   139  of; Colombia; Costa Rica; Dominican Republic; Egypt; El Salvador; 
   140  Guatemala; Guyana; Honduras; Hong Kong, China; India; Iraq; Israel; 
   141  Japan; Jordan; Kazakhstan; Kuwait; Libya; Malaysia; Morocco; New 
   142  Zealand; Nicaragua; Nigeria; Norway; Oman; Peru; the Philippines; 
   143  Qatar; Russia; Saudi Arabia; Singapore; South Africa; South Korea; Sri 
   144  Lanka; Switzerland; Taiwan; Thailand; Trinidad and Tobago; 
   145  T[uuml]rkiye; United Arab Emirates; United Kingdom; Uruguay; Venezuela; 
   146  and Vietnam.
   147       The following six economies have failed to effectively 
   148  enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced 
   149  labor: Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and 
   150  Pakistan.
   151       All of the investigated economies have failed to impose a 
   152  forced labor import prohibition and to effectively enforce such a 
   153  prohibition (that is to say, all of the economies have failed to 
   154  satisfy both factors in these investigations).
   155      The Trade Representative proposed to determine that action is 
   156  appropriate in each investigation, and that appropriate action would 
   157  include tariffs on all products of an economy, with certain exemptions. 
   158  The Trade Representative also proposed a textile mechanism that would 
   159  allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports from certain 
   160  economies to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff 
   161  rate. See 91 FR 34272 (published June 5, 2026) (the June 5, 2026 FRN).
   162      The June 5, 2026 FRN invited public comments on the proposed 
   163  actions to be taken in each investigation. The June 5, 2026 FRN 
   164  proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a 
   165  forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments related to 
   166  forced labor import prohibitions through an ART; or has imposed a 
   167  partial regime with the effect of preventing the importation of certain 
   168  forced labor goods. The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 
   169  12.5 percent for every other economy. The tariff proposals in each 
   170  investigation included exemptions for certain goods, including 
   171  informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, all articles 
   172  and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232 of the Trade 
   173  Expansion Act of 1962, and certain products identified in Annex A to 
   174  the June 5, 2026 FRN.
   175      As explained in the June 5, 2026 FRN, the proposed exemptions 
   176  included: (a) raw materials that, if subject to the proposed additional 
   177  tariffs, could lead to the unavailability of domestic supply; (b) 
   178  products that could cause economy-wide disruptions if subject to 
   179  additional tariffs; (c) certain products that cannot be grown or 
   180  produced in sufficient quantities in the United States or obtained from 
   181  other sources; and (d) articles for which additional tariffs may not 
   182  contribute substantially to the elimination of the acts, policies, and 
   183  practices determined to be actionable in the investigations.
   184      Interested persons were invited to provide comments regarding the 
   185  scope
   186  
   187  [[Page 47319]]
   188  
   189  of tariff coverage (including the proposed excluded products identified 
   190  in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN and the proposed textile mechanism. 
   191  With respect to the tariff proposals, the June 5, 2026 FRN stated that, 
   192  in considering whether certain articles should be subject to additional 
   193  duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act, USTR will consider the needs 
   194  of the U.S. economy. With respect to comments on the inclusion or 
   195  removal of particular tariff subheadings subject to the proposed 
   196  action, USTR requested that comments address specifically whether the 
   197  products under the tariff subheading are necessary raw materials that 
   198  if subject to the proposed tariff could lead to the unavailability of 
   199  domestic supply; whether additional tariffs would cause serious 
   200  dislocations in the supply of the products and could cause economy-wide 
   201  disruptions, or other similar factors; and whether imposing additional 
   202  tariffs on products under the tariff subheading would be practicable or 
   203  effective in obtaining the elimination of the investigated acts, 
   204  policies, and practices.
   205      USTR also requested public comments regarding the proposed actions, 
   206  including whether the products in Annex A to the June 5, 2026 FRN were 
   207  appropriately excluded; the level of the increase, if any, in the rate 
   208  of duty; whether differential tariff rates should be applied to an 
   209  economy where the economy has made a commitment to the United States to 
   210  impose and enforce a forced labor import prohibition, has imposed a 
   211  forced labor import prohibition, or has imposed a partial regime with 
   212  the effect of preventing the importation of certain forced labor goods; 
   213  and features of the proposed textile mechanism, including the U.S. and 
   214  foreign products to be covered, the relative market opportunities for 
   215  each side, and the tariff rate (if any) to be applied to products 
   216  subject to the mechanism, as well as whether a similar mechanism should 
   217  apply to any other product or sector.
   218      In response to the June 5, 2026 FRN, USTR received over 1,600 
   219  written comments. USTR and the Section 301 Committee held a three-day 
   220  public hearing on July 7, 8, and 9, 2026, regarding the proposed 
   221  actions. During the hearings, over 100 witnesses provided testimony and 
   222  responded to questions. Witnesses included representatives of the 
   223  governments of certain investigated economies, industry associations, 
   224  domestic producers, and non-governmental organizations. The public 
   225  submissions are available at: https://comments.ustr.gov/s/ at docket 
   226  numbers USTR-2026-0265 and USTR-2026-0266. Transcripts of the hearings 
   227  are available on USTR's website.
   228      Following government-to-government consultations pursuant to 
   229  Section 303 of the Trade Act and the publication of proposed actions in 
   230  the June 5, 2026 FRN, additional economies have imposed forced labor 
   231  import prohibitions--Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, 
   232  and Trinidad and Tobago; or undertaken commitments regarding forced 
   233  labor import prohibitions in an ART--Jordan.
   234  
   235  II. Determinations of Action
   236  
   237  A. Overview of Responsive Actions in the Investigations
   238  
   239      On June 2, 2026, the Trade Representative determined that, in each 
   240  of the 60 investigations, certain acts, policies, and practices of the 
   241  economy at issue are unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. commerce, 
   242  and are thus actionable under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act. Section 
   243  301(b) provides that upon determining that the acts, policies, and 
   244  practices under investigation are actionable and that action is 
   245  appropriate, the Trade Representative shall take all appropriate and 
   246  feasible action authorized under Section 301(c), subject to the 
   247  specific direction, if any, of the President regarding such action, and 
   248  all other appropriate and feasible action within the power of the 
   249  President that the President may direct the Trade Representative to 
   250  take under Section 301(b), to obtain the elimination of that act, 
   251  policy, or practice. Section 301(b) provides further that actions 
   252  ``within the power of the President'' may include ``[a]ctions . . . 
   253  with respect to trade in any goods or services, or with respect to any 
   254  other area of pertinent relations with the foreign country.''
   255      Section 301(c) of the Trade Act authorizes the Trade Representative 
   256  to take certain, specific actions for purposes of carrying out the 
   257  provisions of Section 301(b). For example, Section 301(c)(1)(B) 
   258  authorizes the Trade Representative to ``impose duties or other import 
   259  restrictions on the goods'' of the foreign country subject to the 
   260  investigation. Section 301(c)(3)(A) provides that actions that the 
   261  Trade Representative is authorized to take may be taken against any 
   262  goods or economic sector on a non-discriminatory basis or solely 
   263  against the foreign country concerned. Section 301(c)(3)(B) empowers 
   264  the Trade Representative to take actions against any goods and economic 
   265  sector ``without regard to whether or not such goods or economic sector 
   266  were involved in the act, policy, or practice that is the subject of 
   267  such action.''
   268      USTR and the Section 301 Committee have carefully reviewed the 
   269  public comments and testimony regarding the proposed actions to be 
   270  taken in each investigation. The Trade Representative informed the 
   271  President of his recommended responsive actions in each investigation, 
   272  including, for each economy, whether to impose 10 or 12.5 percent 
   273  tariffs on all products of that economy or, in the case of specific 
   274  economies, 10 or 12.5 percent tariffs net of a product's MFN duty, with 
   275  exemptions for certain goods. The Trade Representative also informed 
   276  the President of economies that have imposed forced labor import 
   277  prohibitions, or undertaken commitments regarding forced labor import 
   278  prohibitions through an ART, since June 5, 2026. The Trade 
   279  Representative also advised the President that, after considering 
   280  significant comments and testimony on the proposed actions, certain 
   281  products warranted exemption from the tariffs imposed in the 
   282  investigations as they are: (a) raw materials that if subject to these 
   283  tariffs could lead to the unavailability of domestic supply; (b) 
   284  products that could cause economy-wide disruptions if subject to these 
   285  tariffs; (c) products that cannot be grown or produced in sufficient 
   286  quantities or at reasonable prices in the United States or obtained 
   287  from other sources; (d) products for which these tariffs may not be 
   288  effective in obtaining the elimination of the acts, policies, and 
   289  practices of economies found to be actionable in the investigations; or 
   290  (e) certain products of Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El 
   291  Salvador, the European Union, Guatemala, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, 
   292  Switzerland, Taiwan, or the United Kingdom that would encourage these 
   293  economies to fulfill commitments regarding forced labor import 
   294  prohibitions or to encourage these economies to enact and effectively 
   295  enforce a forced labor import prohibition.
   296      On July 23, 2026--after considering and taking account of the 
   297  information and advice provided by the Trade Representative; the 
   298  information, findings, and determinations in the June 5, 2026 FRN; the

   305  provided in this memorandum, the Trade Representative shall impose

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty
